obligations.note: Mechanism 14 (numeric verbatim). Harm when a summary line names a campaign and states one of its source numbers (ctr, clicks, impressions; spend for Holiday 2024) with the same value but not verbatim (amount match AND NOT verbatim match, e.g. 0.60 for 0.6, $8,420 for 8420.0). Conditional rule: omitting the number is fine. Interpretation call: the prompt's 'verbatim (don't paraphrase or round)' is read literally for numbers too. Not detected: values on a different line from the name; a rounded value (different number, e.g. 0.6 for 0.59) cannot be attributed without labels; 'value,' is missed (defect amount-followed-by-comma).

mechanism_defects.summary: mentions amount mode misses a number directly followed by a comma: _NUMBER (src/automationbench_v1/contracts/predicates.py:503) matches '$8,420,' greedily ([\d,]*), the token then fails to parse and the line is decided false. 'spend $8,420, no sign-off' -> False although 8420 is present; 'spend $8,420.' and '(spend $8,420)' -> True. Obligations using amount can return a false 0 for a correct report written as 'X, Y'; guards miss the harm. Fix sketch: exclude a trailing comma from the token (e.g. \d(?:[\d,]*\d)?).

mentions amount / amount_reformatted on a raw JSON-number field (ctr 0.6, spend 8420.0) is silently unknown (predicate_mentions_value_unavailable, src/automationbench_v1/contracts/predicates.py _prepare: _decimal rejects non-strings; amount_reformatted needs source text). Workaround used: amount over a derived {input format number}, and 'reformatted' = amount AND NOT verbatim (numeric verbatim renders 0.6 as '0.6').

limitations: Numeric-verbatim guard reads name and number on one line; other layouts are false negatives, never false harms.
Amount matching misses numbers followed by a comma (defect); affects the average-CTR obligation too (false 0 possible).
The campaign-deleted guard has no simulator tool path today (status REMOVED is the removal path); it closes api_fetch deletes.
Outcome-only checks; no credit rules are declared.
